*[Bug 19114] New: poison free small-node data to catch use of collected objects*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19114>

            Bug ID: 19114
           Summary: poison free small-node data to catch use of collected
                    objects
           Product: R
           Version: R 4.6.x
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3765
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3765&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

This patch provided an additional mechanism for identifying usages of
unprotected objects, via ASan's support for "poisoning" of memory regions.

In short, once a memory region has been "poisoned", ASan can then report an
error if that memory region is accessed or used. This is primarily helpful in
identifying usages of unprotected (or already-freed) R objects, which might
otherwise be challenging to isolate via e.g. `gctorture()`.

With R configured as `CC="clang -fsanitize=address"
CFLAGS="-fno-omit-frame-pointer -g -O2" MAIN_LDFLAGS=-fsanitize=address` (no
strict barrier needed), running this under `gctorture(TRUE)`:

```
SEXP C_uaf(void)
{
    SEXP x = allocVector(REALSXP, 3);
    REAL(x)[0] = 42.0;
    SEXP y = PROTECT(allocVector(REALSXP, 100)); /* x not protected */
    double d = REAL(x)[0];  /* use after collection */
    REAL(y)[0] = d;
    UNPROTECT(1);
    return y;
}
```

produces an immediate report with the exact faulting access:

```
==13131==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: use-after-poison on address 0x625001a5b938
...
    #0 0x000101d7d2f4 in C_uaf uaf.c:13
    #1 0x00010105ec10 in R_doDotCall dotcode.c:751
    #2 0x00010106feb0 in do_dotcall dotcode.c:1437
    #3 0x0001010f1ab0 in Rf_eval eval.c:1258
    ...
```

*[Bug 19115] New: `do_pmatch()` never protects its hash table*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19115>

            Bug ID: 19115
           Summary: `do_pmatch()` never protects its hash table
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3766
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3766&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

To reproduce:

```
n   <- 101L                                   # > 100 on both sides
pad <- rawToChar(as.raw(rep(0xe9, 500)))      # 500 high bytes, unmarked
tab <- paste0(pad, sprintf("%04d", seq_len(n)))
Encoding(tab) <- rep("latin1", n)             # declared encoding => useUTF8
gctorture(TRUE)
pmatch(tab, tab)
```

This gives me a crash with R 4.6.1 on macOS:

```
> n   <- 101L                                   # > 100 on both sides
pad <- rawToChar(as.raw(rep(0xe9, 500)))      # 500 high bytes, unmarked
tab <- paste0(pad, sprintf("%04d", seq_len(n)))
Encoding(tab) <- rep("latin1", n)             # declared encoding => useUTF8
gctorture(TRUE)
pmatch(tab, tab)> pad <- rawToChar(as.raw(rep(0xe9, 500)))      # 500 high
bytes, unmarked
> tab <- paste0(pad, sprintf("%04d", seq_len(n)))
> Encoding(tab) <- rep("latin1", n)             # declared encoding => useUTF8
> gctorture(TRUE)
> pmatch(tab, tab)

 *** caught bus error ***
address 0xbb4642130, cause 'invalid alignment'

Traceback:
 1: pmatch(tab, tab)
```

*[Bug 19116] New: <matrix>[[i, j]]: stochastic error with negative i*
<https://bugs.r-project.org/show_bug.cgi?id=19116>

            Bug ID: 19116
           Summary: <matrix>[[i, j]]: stochastic error with negative i
           Product: R
           Version: R-devel (trunk)
          Hardware: Other
                OS: Other
            Status: NEW
          Severity: normal
          Priority: P5
         Component: Low-level
          Assignee: <mailto:R-core@R-project.org|R-core@R-project.org>
          Reporter: <mailto:kevinushey@gmail.com|kevinushey@gmail.com>

Created attachment 3767
  --> <https://bugs.r-project.org/attachment.cgi?id=3767&action=edit>
Candidate patch.

To reproduce:

```
m <- matrix(1:4, 2)

mm <- m; mm[[-1, 1]] <- 99L
mm[, 1]

## `[[` reads an uninitialized int in the same argument position:
res <- replicate(200, {
  invisible(lapply(1:200, function(i) c(2L, 2L)))   # churn the heap
  tryCatch(as.character(m[[-1, 1]]), error = function(e) "<error>")
})
table(res)
```

This gives me:

```
> mm <- m; mm[[-1, 1]] <- 99L
> mm[, 1]
[1]  1 99
>
> ## `[[` reads an uninitialized int in the same argument position:
> res <- replicate(200, {
+   invisible(lapply(1:200, function(i) c(2L, 2L)))   # churn the heap
+   tryCatch(as.character(m[[-1, 1]]), error = function(e) "<error>")
+ })
> table(res)
res
<error>       2
    173      27
```

but note that the number of errors here isn't deterministic.

From what I can see, the issue here arises because of the use of `pindx`
instead of `pdims` in the invocation of `get1index()`. Note that the same loop
form is used in `do_subassign2_dflt()` (`subassign.c:1897-1911`), but with
`pdims[i]` passed instead, so I suspect this is a long-standing typo.
